sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a house in Calumet City?
sections.html:
A Calumet City owner can list the house, sell it without an agent, or sell directly to a cash buyer. Just over half of the city's housing is owner-occupied, and about one in ten housing units was vacant in the 2020 census, so many sellers are landlords, heirs or owners of houses that have sat empty.

  • Listing: reaches the broadest set of buyers, though lenders will want repairs and inspections handled.
  • Private sale: saves the commission and leaves the city paperwork to you.
  • Cash buyer: suits houses with deferred repairs, tenants in place, or an estate that needs to close quickly.

All three routes need the city's real estate transfer stamp and a paid final water bill, covered below.

sections.h2: What is Calumet City and where is it?
sections.html:
Calumet City, called "Cal City" locally, sits in Cook County's Thornton Township on the Indiana state line. It covers 7.32 square miles and borders Hammond to the east, Burnham and Chicago to the north, Lansing to the south, and South Holland and Dolton to the west.

The city began in 1893 when the villages of Schrumville and Sobieski Park merged as West Hammond. Prohibition in Indiana turned it into a drinking destination, which earned the nickname "Sin City." Residents voted in 1923 to adopt the Calumet City name, and in 1995 the city began demolishing the bars along the old "Sin Strip." Today two water towers painted as smiley faces, near River Oaks Mall and along State Street near Interstate 94, are a local landmark.

The city's 2020 census count was 36,033. The Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 34,798, down 3.5 percent from the 2020 base.

sections.html:
The Census Bureau lists a median owner-occupied home value of $145,200 for Calumet City and an owner-occupied rate of 55.7 percent. Median gross rent is $1,177, and median household income is $55,369.

sections.h2: What does the Calumet City transfer stamp cost?
sections.html:
The City Clerk's Real Estate Transfer Declaration prints a stamp cost of $4.00 per $1,000 or part thereof as the buyer's expense, and another $4.00 per $1,000 or part thereof as the seller's, for a total of $8.00 per $1,000 or part thereof. The form covers transfers up to and including $2 million.

  • Pick up stamps at least 48 hours ahead and allow about half an hour to process.
  • Pay by certified check, money order or cash only.
  • The person requesting must be the owner of record, an attorney or a broker, with a bar or license number written on the form.
  • Exempt transfers cite a paragraph of Sec. 82-323 of the city's municipal code, and a copy of the deed must be submitted.

The Office of the City Clerk is reached at (708) 891-8110, Monday to Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The form lists the property's township as Thornton and ZIP code 60409.

sections.h2: How do I handle the final water bill in Calumet City?
sections.html:
The seller, or the seller's representative, must order a final water meter reading at least 48 hours before buying the transfer stamp, and all outstanding water bills must be paid before a property is sold. To schedule the reading, call Water Billing at (708) 891-8121.

The Water Service Information page prints these monthly rates under Utilities Ordinance 26-01, and says water rates rise automatically in step with Chicago or Hammond water increases:

  • Water: $11.45 per 1,000 gallons.
  • Sewer: $1.33 per 1,000 gallons.
  • Stormwater: $2.00 per 1,000 gallons or part thereof.
  • Refuse: $31.30 per unit, with a $15.65 senior rate for the first unit at age 65.

The city says it draws all of its drinking water from Lake Michigan. New owners must file a water service application, and a security deposit may be required in some cases.

sections.h2: What rental and vacant-property rules does Calumet City have?
sections.html:
Calumet City's Forms & Applications page lists a rental application, an annual rental code compliance letter, an owner-occupied form, a Crime Free Housing licensing application and a vacant and foreclosed property registration. If the house you want to sell is a rental, ask the city whether the rental license and compliance letter are current, since a buyer's attorney will ask for them.

Ask Building & Zoning whether the vacant and foreclosed property registration applies to your house. The Building & Zoning office, (708) 891-8120, takes permit applications for building, electrical, plumbing, HVAC and fences, and there is an overhead sewer rebate program form on the same page. Ask the office whether any open permits or violations attach to the address before you list.

Calling the Building & Zoning office before you accept an offer can prevent a surprise after the buyer's inspection.

sections.h2: What state and county steps apply in Calumet City?
sections.html:
The deed is recorded with the Cook County Clerk's Recordings Division, whose offices are open 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. with the last customer accepted at 4:45 p.m. Buyer and seller also complete the PTAX-203 Illinois Real Estate Transfer Declaration.

Illinois's own tax is 50 cents per $500 of value, and counties may add 25 cents per $500. Home rule municipalities may add their own, which is the category the city stamp falls into.

For the Cook County tax bill, the Assessor says exemptions appear as deductions on the second installment bill. Ask the Cook County Treasurer for the amounts and due dates on your parcel.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about the area around Calumet City?
sections.html:
Calumet City's neighbors include Hammond, Lansing, Dolton and South Holland, which means buyers often compare a Calumet City house with homes across several municipal lines. The Census Bureau puts the average commute at 34.4 minutes, so a listing that explains transit and highway access helps.

Calumet City's Public Works number is (708) 891-8161, and the clerk and the water offices are the first stops for a buyer taking over a house. Giving a buyer those three numbers up front can speed the handover.

A cash buyer who is comfortable with tenants in place, an older furnace or an overhead sewer can sometimes close faster than a buyer who needs a loan, while a retail buyer will pay more for a house that has been updated.

faqs.q: What does the Calumet City transfer stamp cost?
faqs.a: The clerk's form prints $4.00 per $1,000 or part thereof for the buyer and $4.00 for the seller, $8.00 per $1,000 or part thereof in total, for transfers up to and including $2 million.

faqs.q: How do I order a final water reading in Calumet City?
faqs.a: Call Water Billing at (708) 891-8121. The city says to order it at least 48 hours before you buy the stamp, and all water bills must be paid before the property is sold.

faqs.q: How can I pay for the transfer stamp?
faqs.a: With a certified check, money order or cash only, according to the Real Estate Transfer Declaration. Plan to pick the stamps up at least 48 hours ahead.

faqs.q: Who records a Calumet City deed?
faqs.a: The Cook County Clerk's Recordings Division, because the city is in Cook County. The recording office takes customers until 4:45 p.m.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Calumet City rental house?
faqs.a: Yes. The city has rental application and annual compliance letter forms, so confirm both are in order, and ask Building & Zoning at (708) 891-8120 about open permits before you sign a contract.
